Adjacent aggregate Load-to-Store forwarding discriminator, recorded before implementation:
The production library stays at the running-index source from3b654f6a6. Test a general backend optimization: a stored aggregate load used exactly once by the immediately following store can transfer directly from source address to destination, with memmove for general overlap and the existing equal-or-disjoint memcpy permission for the closed swap row. No intervening IR operation or other use can observe a snapshot; all other loads remain snapshots. Do not extend forwarding across calls, writes, blocks, scheduling joins, exposed backing or runtime-content representations. Omit the eliminated temporary before target frame qualification.
The native discriminator requires the generic aggregate swap row to reduce two temporaries/four copies to one/three while preserving same-place exchange and source snapshots where any premise fails. Inspect optimized complete reached HashMap paths, not raw copy count alone.
Compile and measure the unchanged production mutation witness with baseline and compiler-only candidate under the existing driver, runtime/peer objects, seeds, work and two-cohort comparison; preserve complete payload work, independent controls, accounting and every sample. Retain only repeatable relevant improvement with no separated regression in this panel, then expand formal correctness and existing container controls before selecting generally. An inconclusive/loss result is evidence against selection, not permission to weaken the criterion. This does not reinstate the rejected direct-field library candidate or inactive enum clearing.
